decisions.reason: As a flexible cardboard display close to the firm's core capabilities, it likely meets a tolerable aspiration level and a large firm has enough slack to keep it despite limited recent public evidence.

This pegboard-backed cardboard display is still closely related to the established display business, so boundedly rational management would be inclined to retain it unless internal results clearly fell below aspiration.
A standard cardboard quarter-pallet display fits the firm's main product logic well, making it a comparatively safe variant to continue while resources remain available.
The eighth-pallet format is somewhat narrower in application, but it remains within the firm's core display segment and would likely be kept unless its sales persistently underperformed peers.

The wooden display pallet is less aligned with a paper-products manufacturer’s main competencies, so if results were only modest management would more readily reallocate resources to better-fitting products or new projects.
A quarter-pallet display tailored to media products serves a narrower and potentially weaker segment, so a shortfall versus aspiration would likely trigger problemistic search and withdrawal.
